stories.title: Instagram and Facebook will likely require a redesign after EU rules they’re ‘addictive’
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Meta faces potential redesigns for Instagram and Facebook due to alleged 'addictive' design features.
The issue stems from a preliminary investigation finding Meta in breach of the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA).
The company risks substantial penalties, including a fine of up to $12 billion, from the European Commission.

stories.title: GPT-5.6
stories.author: logickkk1
bullet_points: The news pertains to the release or documentation of 'GPT-5.6' from OpenAI.
The content links point to official OpenAI deployment safety documents and API guides, indicating a formal release or update.
This represents significant news in the rapidly evolving field of large language models (LLMs).

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown

It pertains to the core area of text generation using transformer models.

bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these agents to run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool aims to bridge the gap between messaging platforms and local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: Would you host part of an AI data center in your home?
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Sunrun is piloting a 'distributed AI compute' program, moving beyond traditional centralized data centers.
The program incentivizes homeowners to host compute units for the solar/energy storage company.
This represents a novel shift in AI infrastructure by leveraging residential energy and computing resources.

stories.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a new tool, rebranded as Codex, aimed at automating and assisting user workflows.
The new tool is designed to support independent, long-running processes, capable of operating for extended periods.
This signals a move toward more autonomous and integrated AI assistants capable of handling complex, sustained tasks.

stories.title: Humanoid robots controlled by surgeons did world-first operation on live pigs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Humanoid robots are being tested for use in surgical procedures.
The trial involved a world-first operation performed on live pigs.
The research aims to assess the feasibility of robotic assistance in surgery.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video understanding.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving perception and safety assessment.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Quantization in LLMs is commonly used for deployment but current evaluation metrics (accuracy, perplexity) are insufficient.
The research introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to assess behavioral changes post-quantization.
This metric measures the overlap in correct predictions between a base model and its quantized versions, independent of absolute accuracy.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: ARDY introduces a new autoregressive diffusion model for generating realistic 3D human motions.
The research addresses the critical trade-off between the high controllability of offline methods and the real-time inference speed needed for interactive applications.
The model aims to bridge the gap by enabling fast, controllable, and semantically rich motion synthesis for robotics and animation.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents operating in real-world tasks.
Addresses limitations in current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluation.
Aims to provide a more granular and effective evaluation framework for complex, real-world agent capabilities.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
It addresses the constraint of single ReAct agents being limited by trajectory length and context window when handling deep and wide research tasks.
The system aims to improve upon existing multi-agent methods by specifically enhancing recursive search depth and coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations of existing refinement techniques (like rule-based methods) regarding quality and efficiency.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory.
Proposes MAESTRO, a new method to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Highlights that existing pruning methods fail because they ignore the interdependent routing nature of MoE architectures.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Instagram’s Adam Mosseri: If you don’t like AI, ‘then you shouldn’t have it in your feed’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Instagram head Adam Mosseri advocates against filtering out AI-generated content on the platform.
Mosseri suggests that users who dislike AI content should actively manage their feeds rather than relying on platform filtering.
The discussion highlights the ongoing debate regarding content moderation and the integration of generative AI into social media feeds.

stories.title: Xreal’s new AR glasses are way cheaper and almost just right
stories.author: Cameron Faulkner
bullet_points: Xreal has released a more affordable AR glasses model, the A01 Plus, priced at $299.
The A01 Plus is a stripped-down version of the higher-end $449 1S model.
The new glasses are praised for being comfortable, aesthetically pleasing, and having surprisingly good screens.

stories.title: Polestar owners left ‘holding the bag’ after EV brand pulls out of the US
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Polestar has withdrawn its operations from the US market.
The withdrawal followed the federal government denying authorization due to a rule against vehicles with Chinese-made connected vehicle software.
The decision highlights regulatory hurdles and supply chain risks for international EV manufacturers in the US.

stories.title: Microsoft’s carbon emissions went up 25 percent last year
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft's carbon emissions reportedly increased by 25% in 2025, according to its 2026 sustainability report.
The increase occurred 'without select interventions,' suggesting challenges in meeting climate targets.
The rise in emissions was primarily attributed to the company's expansion.

stories.title: Fidji Simo steps down from leading OpenAI’s AGI work due to illness
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI's AGI Chief, Fidji Simo, is stepping down from her full-time leadership role.
The transition is due to ongoing health issues, specifically a neuroimmune condition.
Simo will remain affiliated with OpenAI as a part-time advisor.

stories.title: Netflix reportedly considers adding always-on channels
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly exploring the addition of always-on streaming channels.
This feature would allow continuous streaming of specific content, similar to Pluto TV or Tubi.
The key differentiator for Netflix would be its paid, ad-supported model, unlike the free, ad-supported competitors.

stories.title: The ChatGPT browser is already dead
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI is discontinuing ChatGPT Atlas, a browser-based feature designed to perform tasks on the user's behalf.
The shutdown occurs less than a year after Atlas was initially announced in October.
This move is part of a broader announcement regarding ChatGPT Work features.

stories.title: Patch for Windows Defender 0-day could allow attackers to fill hard disk
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A zero-day vulnerability in Windows Defender has been identified.
Exploitation of this flaw could potentially allow attackers to fill a hard disk.
The ongoing conflict between NightmareEclipse and Microsoft regarding the issue remains unresolved.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a temporal alternative to traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT) methods.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for complex CoF reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI systems' ability to reason about scientific lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking both scientific lineage reasoning and the generation of new ideas grounded in prior work.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across a massive dataset of 77,543 distance learning students, segmented by demographics.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent, conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows.
The model utilizes Lisp-inspired concepts like symbolic forms and object identity to explain workflow persistence.
Addresses the need for better semantic persistence across complex LLM workflows involving tool use and branching.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on moral foundation tasks compared to much larger open models.
The paper raises a critical academic point: high agreement (reliability) does not guarantee true validity when inferring theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: Addresses a gap between accurate 3D human pose estimation and the need for biomechanical insights (e.g., loading, activation).
Introduces 'BioModule,' a lightweight plug-in temporal transformer designed to bridge this gap.
Applicable to diverse fields including rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper investigates the limitations of using forward diffusion marginal error to guarantee numerical stability in diffusion sampling.
It demonstrates that a small $L^2$ error in the forward marginal does not ensure the learned reverse-time process is numerically stable.
The research shows that a smooth score field can be constructed with minimal forward error while maintaining a nonexplosive and stable reverse-time process.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final low-dimensional projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this pre-projection graph can enhance data sensemaking and analysis.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—individual parameters critical to model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training will improve models, showing the opposite effect.
Demonstrates that isolating and training these critical parameters drastically reduces LLM accuracy.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
The authors introduce 'BioModule,' a lightweight plug-in temporal transformer designed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The work is relevant to fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis by enabling functional movement analysis from pose data.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of translating flexible, language-based reasoning into continuous control policies for robotics/AI.
Proposes a novel architecture, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing Autoregressive Variational Inference.
Aims to provide the necessary granularity for spatial understanding and precise motor control, bridging language models and physical action.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses limitations of existing methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The paper cautions that agreement (reliability) does not guarantee validity for complex, inferred theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in growing trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over extended timeframes.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning, specifically for citation verification.
It focuses on the calibration and bias of LLMs when assessing citation quality in deep-research systems that require source attribution for every claim.
This research is relevant to improving the trustworthiness and reliability of advanced, search-grounded LLMs.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'DominoTree,' an advancement in speculative decoding for LLM inference.
Domino addresses limitations of existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction into the drafter.
This new structure allows the draft token's distribution path to be dependent, which was previously unrepresentable in factorized tree formulations.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053) to address limitations in current LLM evaluation.
Highlights the significant variability in communication patterns and emotional expression among real patients.
Introduces a novel patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotion, strategy, and communication.

stories.title: Cpp2Rust: Automatic Translation of C++ to Safe Rust
stories.author: github.com via gnyeki
bullet_points: Cpp2Rust aims to automatically translate code from C++ to Rust.
The project focuses on enabling safer code by leveraging Rust's memory safety features.
This addresses the growing need for interoperability and modernization between C++ and Rust ecosystems.

stories.title: I Built a Linter That Catches the Security Bugs AI Assistants Keep Writing
stories.author: ri5hu
bullet_points: The article discusses the increasing use of AI assistants (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) in software development.
The author developed a custom linter specifically designed to identify security vulnerabilities introduced by AI-generated code.
This highlights a growing industry concern regarding the security risks associated with relying on generative AI for coding tasks.

stories.title: Are You Using Coding Agents Like Slot Machines?
stories.author: loicboset
bullet_points: Coding agents are significantly accelerating development time, reducing hours of work to minutes.
The article discusses the increasing pressure on companies to adopt AI technologies.
The title uses a provocative metaphor ('Slot Machines') to question the effective or strategic use of these agents.

stories.title: Multimodal Models Don't Fail at Understanding. They Fail at Sampling
stories.author: aiexplore369zoho
bullet_points: The article suggests that failures in multimodal AI applications are often not due to inherent model understanding limitations.
The core issue identified is related to 'sampling decisions' made during model operation.
This points to a critical gap between impressive multimodal demos and reliable production-level deployment.

stories.title: Give Your AI Assistant a Private Memory
stories.author: asciimoo
bullet_points: Introduces Hister MCP, a tool enabling AI assistants to access private user data.
Allows AI assistants to search personal reading history and stored previews.
Focuses on building a private, indexed knowledge base for personalized AI interaction.
